title: Bit-flip on Alice's special coordinate preserves volume
statement: Fix a positive integer $n$, and consider the finite sample space whose points are the hard samples $\omega = (T, x_T, y_T, \mathrm{other})$, with $T \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, bits $x_T, y_T \in \{\text{false}, \text{true}\}$, and a coordinate labelling $\mathrm{other} \colon \{0,\dots,n-1\} \to \{\text{neither}, \text{leftOnly}, \text{rightOnly}\}$. Let $f$ be the self-map of this space that toggles Alice's special-coordinate bit, sending $\omega$ to $(T, \lnot x_T, y_T, \mathrm{other})$ while leaving $T$, $y_T$, and $\mathrm{other}$ fixed. Then $f$ is measure-preserving for the volume (uniform counting) measure on the finite sample space: it is measurable and pushes the volume measure forward to itself.
hypotheses_covered: n is a positive natural number
the map flips only the special bit x_T (negation), keeping T, y_T, other fixed
conclusion: the map is measure-preserving from volume to volume on the finite sample space
